title: "_mapmaking"

## Install & load packages

```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

source("../R/strip_lat_lon_fr_pt.R")
```

## Map with coordinates: World

```{r}
#| label: fetch-world-map
# Fetch world map data as an 'sf' object
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Plot the map
ggplot(data = world) +
  geom_sf()
```

## Map three cities

```{r}
#| label: plot-basic-map
#| 
# A standard data frame with coordinates
cities_df <- data.frame(
  city = c("New York", "Paris", "Tokyo"),
  lon = c(-74.0060, 2.3522, 139.6503),
  lat = c(40.7128, 48.8566, 35.6762)
)

# Convert to an sf object (4326 is the standard GPS CRS, WGS84)
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_df, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# Layer the points over the base map
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "antiquewhite", color = "gray80") +
  geom_sf(data = cities_sf, color = "red", size = 3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-100, 150), ylim = c(-20, 60)) # Zooming into an area
```

## Getting states

```{r}
#| label: get-states
us_states <- ne_states(country = "United States of America")
```

## Map my location

```{r}
#| label: fig-my-location
cities_df <- data.frame(
  city = c("State College"),
  lon = c(-77.84922),
  lat = c(40.79766)
)

# Convert to an sf object (4326 is the standard GPS CRS, WGS84)
cities_sf <- st_as_sf(cities_df, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = "antiquewhite", color = "gray80") +
  geom_sf(data = cities_sf, color = "red", size = 1) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-80.5, -74.8), ylim = c(39.5, 42.5)) # Zooming into an area
```

## Import PA higher ed data

```{r}
#| label: import-higher-ed-data
pa_higher_ed <- readr::read_csv("../include/xlsx/PA_Higher_Education_Institutions_by_Sector_Current_Statewide_Education_20261015.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

summary(pa_higher_ed)
```

## Trim the data

```{r}
#| label: trim-higher-ed
pa_higher_ed_trimmed <- pa_higher_ed |>
  rename(lon = Longitude,
         lat = Latitude) |>
  select(Sector, College, Type, County, lon, lat) |>
  filter(!is.na(lat) &
         !is.na(lon))

```


```{r}
#| label: convert-higher-ed-data
# Convert to an sf object (4326 is the standard GPS CRS, WGS84)

pa_higher_ed_sf <-
  sf::st_as_sf(
    x = pa_higher_ed_trimmed,
    coords = c("lon", "lat"),
    crs = 4326
  )
```

## Map the data

```{r}
#| label: fig-pa-higher-ed
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = "antiquewhite", color = "gray80") +
  geom_sf(data = pa_higher_ed_sf, aes(color = Sector), size = 1) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-80.5, -74.8), ylim = c(39.5, 42.5)) # Zooming into an area
```

## *ggmap*

Requires API key. Don't use for class.

## Choropleth

AI suggested

---

```{r}
#| label: get-world-map
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
# Load country shapes (excluding Antarctica for a cleaner view)
world_map <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% 
  filter(name != "Antarctica")
```

---

```{r}
#| label: fig-gdp-map
#| echo: false
#| code-fold: false
#| output-location: slide
ggplot(data = world_map) +
  # Map the color fill to GDP, and draw light white borders between regions
  geom_sf(aes(fill = gdp_md), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  
  # Apply a colorblind-friendly continuous color scale
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "GDP (Millions)", labels = scales::comma_format()) +
  
  # Remove background grid lines and latitude/longitude labels
  theme_void() +
  
  # Add titles
  labs(
    title = "Global GDP Choropleth Map",
    subtitle = "Created using ggplot2 and sf in R",
    caption = "Source: Natural Earth"
  ) +
  
  # Position the legend at the bottom
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# 1. Install and load necessary packages
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Set tigris options to cache shapefiles
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# 2. Get county sf polygon data for a state (e.g., Virginia 'VA')
# Use cb = TRUE for generalized/lighter polygons
county_sf <- counties(state = "VA", cb = TRUE, class = "sf")

# 3. Create or load your sample county-level dataset
# Ensure your county identifier matches the FIPS code ('GEOID' in tigris)
set.seed(123)
county_data <- data.frame(
  GEOID = county_sf$GEOID,
  value = rnorm(nrow(county_sf), mean = 50, sd = 10)
)

# 4. Join the spatial sf object with your data
map_sf <- left_join(county_sf, county_data, by = "GEOID")

# 5. Plot the choropleth map with ggplot2 and geom_sf()
ggplot(data = map_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = value), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Value") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "County-Level Choropleth Map",
    subtitle = "Virginia Counties Colored by Sample Values",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau / tigris"
  )
```

## Map of PA higher ed institutions by county

```{r}
pa_county_sf <- counties(state = "PA", cb = TRUE, class = "sf")
pa_county_sf |> summary()
```

What does the `NAME` variable look like?

```{r}
pa_county_sf$NAME
```

How does this compare with the PA higher ed data?

```{r}
pa_higher_ed_sf$County
```
So, we should be able to merge/join these by `County`.

```{r}
pa_higher_ed_counties <- pa_higher_ed_trimmed |>
  group_by(County) |>
  summarize(n_institutions = n())

pa_map_sf <- left_join(pa_county_sf, pa_higher_ed_counties, join_by(NAME == County))
```

Make the map.

```{r}
ggplot(data = pa_map_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = n_institutions), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  # scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Value") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "County-Level Choropleth Map",
    subtitle = "PA Counties Colored by number of higher ed institutions",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau / tigris"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = pa_map_sf) +
  aes(x = n_institutions) +
  geom_histogram()
```

Based on the histogram, we can create an discrete/ordinal variable for the number of institutions in a county.

```{r}
pa_map_sf |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cut_interval(n_institutions, n = 4)) +
  geom_histogram(stat = "count")
```

```{r}
pa_map_sf_tiers <- pa_map_sf |>
  mutate(
    tier = case_when(
      is.na(n_institutions) ~ "none",
      n_institutions <= 5 ~ "<=5",
      n_institutions <= 10 ~ "6-10",
      n_institutions <= 15 ~ "11-15",
      n_institutions < 21 ~ "16-20"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(tier = ordered(tier, 
                        levels = c("none", "<=5", "6-10", 
                                   "11-15", "16-20")))
```

```{r}
pa_map_sf_tiers |>
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = tier), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  # scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Value") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "County-Level Choropleth Map",
    subtitle = "PA Counties Colored by number of higher ed institutions",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau / tigris"
  )
```
